archetype.name: Game Manager (short-area dependent)
archetype.definition: Daniel Jones is at his best when the Colts' strong run game sets up quick, high-percentage throws to Josh Downs and Keenan Allen; this year that is the only part of his passing that works.

report.headline: The 2025 breakout has unraveled: competent underneath, broken at every other depth.
report.take:
Last year looked like a career reset for Jones. He posted 8.08 yards per attempt, a +2.3 CPOE and 0.193 EPA per play, 11th in the league, in Shane Steichen's offense. Eight games into 2026 he is closer to the Giants version, and worse in some ways. He sits at 5.75 YPA (41st of 47), -0.182 EPA per dropback (39th), nine interceptions and three lost fumbles. The Colts' passing offense ranks 31st in EPA while their run game ranks 5th. The offense is not what's broken. The passing game is.

The depth splits show exactly where it breaks. Under 10 air yards he is fine: 68.8% completions, +0.079 EPA, all five of his touchdowns. Past 10 yards the passing game falls apart. He has hit 4 of 30 deep attempts (13.3%, CPOE -24.4), and five of his nine picks have come on intermediate throws. His aggressiveness is down from 17.7% to 13.43% and his bad-throw rate is up 2.5 points. That reads like a passer who has lost trust in his downfield accuracy. It doesn't look like a scheme that stopped calling deep shots. His career backs that reading: 2025 and 2022 are his only seasons above average in efficiency, and 2023 looked a lot like this one.

The raw totals hide where the damage comes from. Downs and Allen are each above +0.27 EPA per target. Tyler Warren, his third-most targeted player, is at -0.255 across 45 targets, and Jonathan Taylor's targets are negative too. The tight end and backfield looks are draining the passing game. Protection is also part of it. The Colts are 30th in the rate of hits allowed, and over the last three games his sack rate has jumped to 12.4%, including six sacks against a Tennessee defense ranked 24th. The touchdown rate (1.9%) is low enough to bounce back some, but the turnovers come from real bad throws, not bad luck.

The recent slide does come with schedule context. Weeks 7 and 8 came against the 1st- and 3rd-ranked defenses, and he played only 79% of snaps in the 42-7 loss at Jacksonville. Still, the Tennessee game was a bad sign against a soft defense. Without a clear cause, such as a fix on the line or Warren starting to produce, the right expectation is a low-end starter who needs a soft matchup and a pass-heavy game script to put up numbers.

strengths.title: Short game still functions
strengths.body: On throws under 10 air yards he completes 68.8% with positive EPA, and all five of his touchdowns came at that depth. These are rhythm throws off a run game that ranks 5th in EPA, so this part holds up as long as Taylor's ground game does.

strengths.title: Downs and Allen produce
strengths.body: His two main wideouts are both clearly positive per target, at +0.288 and +0.273. When he throws to them the offense works. Leaning more on them is the clearest available fix.

strengths.title: Third-down accuracy holds up
strengths.body: On third down his CPOE is +8.8, far above his season figure. He is accurate on obvious passing downs when the reads are defined. The 7.4 average yards to go keeps the conversion rate modest, but the throwing itself is sound there.

concerns.title: Downfield accuracy has collapsed
concerns.body: He has completed 13.3% of deep throws with a -24.4 CPOE, and five of his nine interceptions came between 10 and 19 yards. His bad-throw rate is up from last year and his aggressiveness is down. That looks like a real accuracy problem, not a few bad bounces, and it is a large part of why YPA fell by 2.33.

concerns.title: Sacks piling up behind a leaky line
concerns.body: The Colts rank 30th in offensive hit rate, and his sack rate over the last three games is 12.4%. Part of this is on the line. Part is on him: his pressure-to-sack rate of 31.1% ranks 25th of 38, so he isn't escaping much either. Ten scrambles all year means his legs aren't offsetting the sacks the way they once did.

concerns.title: Warren targets are a drain
concerns.body: His tight end has drawn 45 targets at -0.255 EPA each, the worst of his top five. Either the usage or the execution on those throws has to change. Otherwise a quarter of his volume keeps working against him.

trend.note: Weeks 2 and 5 were respectable, but every efficiency rate has gotten worse over his last three games: -0.273 EPA per dropback, a 5.4% INT rate and a 12.4% sack rate, all in losses. Two of those came against top-three defenses, which softens the picture without erasing it.

nextGame.headline: Worst pass defense on the schedule, and likely a shootout
nextGame.body:
Dallas has the league's worst defense by EPA, ranks 30th against the pass and 25th in sack rate. It has given up the sixth-most PPR to quarterbacks. Its offense ranks 4th in EPA and the total is 51.5 with Indianapolis a 6-point home underdog, so the Colts probably have to throw a lot. That suits his volume but not his efficiency: trailing by nine or more, he has been at -0.519 EPA per play. Expect yards and attempts above his norm, with turnover risk still attached.

Availability favors him. Safety Caleb Downs, a 93%-snap starter, and P.J. Locke are both in concussion protocol, and linebacker Dee Winters is out. A thin back end is exactly what his broken intermediate and deep game needs to face. On his side, Anthony Gould's concussion barely matters; Gould has not taken offensive snaps. Jones himself practiced fully.

keyMatchups.title: Josh Downs against Dallas WR1 coverage
keyMatchups.body: Dallas has let lead receivers score 6.9 PPR a game over their averages, 31st of 32. Downs is his most efficient target, so feeding him is the obvious path to production.

keyMatchups.title: Weak Dallas rush against Colts protection
keyMatchups.body: Dallas ranks 25th in sack rate, which gives a line ranked 30th in hit rate a rare break. A cleaner pocket is what his drop-off in sacks and bad throws most needs.

keyMatchups.title: Chasing points against a top offense
keyMatchups.body: Dallas's offense is 4th in EPA. If Indianapolis falls behind early, he lands in the game state where he has been worst all year.

nextGame.watch: Whether he completes anything 10+ yards downfield against a Dallas secondary that may be missing both concussed safeties.

restOfSeason.body:
The short passing game, the run support and the Downs/Allen production are real and should keep him around 190-230 passing yards a game, with more against soft defenses like Dallas. The touchdown rate is unusually low and should rise a little toward his career norm. The interceptions come from genuine downfield misses and probably won't drop much unless the bad-throw rate falls back toward last year's.

The 2025 season now looks like his best-case outcome rather than his new baseline. Without a protection fix or a clear jump in his downfield accuracy, expect about 0.7-1.2 touchdown passes and about 1 interception a game. His rushing has faded from his Giants years into short-yardage and goal-line work. Another month like the last three would put his job at risk.
swingFactors: Pass protection and his sack rate
Tyler Warren turning his targets into positive plays

confidence.note: Eight starts is a decent sample, and the depth splits all point the same way. Still, 30 deep throws is a small base, and recent opponents were tough.
